findings.how: Round 1: isTrustedSender reads the URL undecoded, so it can't throw ('100%%20Free' stopped failing every settings request), and autostart execArg doubles % in Exec=. Round 2, verifier #200: I confirmed with a real Electron 44.5 probe that loadFile from a '50%AB' folder fails with ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (-6), while loadURL(pathToFileURL(file).href) loads it ('50%25AB'). It also loads '100% Free' and 'Tools C# 100% Free (x86) & Zoë's [x]', and keeps ?opaque=1. A new plain-Node module, app/main/page-url.ts, has pageUrl(file, query). It builds the URL with pathToFileURL, so % becomes %25 and #, ? and brackets are encoded. All 9 loadFile calls in app/main now use win.loadURL(pageUrl(...)): windows.ts (home, command, prompt), ask.ts (keeps opaque=1), voice.ts (mic, twice), overlay.ts, handle.ts and desk/view.ts. isTrustedSender is unchanged and trusts these URLs. I relabelled the 50%AB unit case to the %25 form Ember now produces, and the raw forms are still checked not to throw. test/smoke/launch.mjs has a new --folder <name> option. It copies dist/app into a temp folder of that name, with the rest of the repository linked beside it (junctions on Windows), and starts Electron with --remote-debugging-port=0. It fails unless the settings page's title is 'Ember'; a page that failed to load has 'index.html' as its title. Cleanup unlinks the links before removing the copy. ci.yml runs it on Linux (as a normal user, sandbox on), on Windows (ASCII name, Git Bash) and on macOS (dev build). Real runs here: the staged/dev build from '50%AB' before the fix showed the home and handle pages titled 'index.html' with 2 ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND. After the fix they are titled 'Ember' with 0 errors. The special folder shows 0 'URI malformed' and 0 handler errors.

The smoke run 'node test/smoke/launch.mjs --folder "Tools C# 100% Free 50%AB (x86) & Zoë's [x]"' failed on the pre-fix build ('its title is "index.html"', ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND in stderr) and passes now. findings.how: Round 1: the Linux doctor probe sees APPIMAGE (sandbox.appImage). With no user namespaces and no setuid helper, an AppImage now gets a warn row ('Ember runs without Chromium's sandbox here…', fix: install the RPM) instead of FAIL with /opt/ember chown advice. Round 2, verifier #202: AppRun in scripts/package/appimage.sh now reads the same two files as doctor-probes.ts. It adds --no-sandbox when /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces is 0 or missing, and also when /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone is 0 (Debian, some hardened Ubuntu). So on a host where the doctor says user namespaces are off, the AppImage really does start without the sandbox, and the doctor's warn and 'Ember can work.' are true.
findings.test: packaging.test.ts 'the launchers': 'start the AppImage without Chromium's sandbox where either switch the doctor reads turns user namespaces off (review #202)' runs the real AppRun against a stand-in /proc/sys. It failed before (max=15000 with clone=0 started with the sandbox) and passes now. It also checks that the AppRun reads exactly those two files. Round 1 cases ('only warns about the sandbox in an AppImage…', platform-linux-system 'say when Ember runs as an AppImage') still pass.

findings.how: Round 1: ember.spec %posttrans prints 'Ember is still running the version before this update: quit Ember and start it again…' when a process runs /opt/ember/ember or '/opt/ember/ember (deleted)'. Round 2, verifier #203: the in-app check is done now. A new plain-Node module, app/main/install-watch.ts, provides installStamp, createUpdateCheck, UPDATED_QUESTION and updatedDetail. At start-up a packaged Ember records its install's package.json (<appPath>/package.json, inode:size:mtime), so a same-version rebuild also counts. A small main.ts hunk calls updateCheck.beforeWindow() on app 'browser-window-created', which covers every window: home, ask, command, prompt, mic, desk, overlay and handle. If the stamp changed, Ember asks once per change with a native dialog: title 'Ember was updated', 'Restart Ember to finish the update.', buttons [Restart Ember] [Not now]. The detail is 'Until it starts again, some of its windows may not work as they should.', or, when tasks, commands or connections are under way, the quit question's words with 'Restarting' ('Ember is connected to build-01. Restarting disconnects.'). Restart calls app.relaunch() then app.quit(). Only one question is open at a time. 'Not now' is asked again only after another change, and a missing file (mid-upgrade) waits. Logged as app.updated_while_running and app.restart_after_update. Limit: the question comes up as the window opens, so that one window can still load the new pages before the user answers. Fully holding the load back would mean gating every window factory before new BrowserWindow, because preloads are read at creation. Real run with the staged Linux tree (first instance --autostart, onboarded): renaming a copy of package.json over the original (as rpm does) and then opening settings logged app.updated_while_running. The control run without the rename asked nothing. The README Linux update line is handed to the docs package (forDocs).
findings.test: test/unit/install-watch.test.ts (new, 7 cases): it asks nothing while the files are unchanged, offers a restart after a new inode and restarts on yes, asks once per update, never asks two at once, waits while the file is missing, asks nothing if the file was unreadable at start-up, and checks the question's words against quitQuestion. It failed before (no module) and passes now. Round 1: packaging.test.ts 'the RPM's upgrade (review #203)' runs the real %posttrans with /bin/sh against a stand-in /proc.

findings.how: ci.yml package job: it restores and verifies the cached real speech models before staging, so rpm.sh also builds ember-voice-models. Then it installs that RPM, runs rpm -V on both, writes an administrator's /etc/ember/policy.json and rebuilds both as Release 2 (EMBER_RPM_RELEASE=2). It dnf-upgrades both, checks the release, runs rpm -V again, checks chrome-sandbox is 4755 root, and runs rpm -e on both. It fails if /opt/ember, /usr/share/ember, /usr/bin/ember, the desktop file or /usr/share/doc/ember is left, or if the policy changed or is owned by a package. Release 2's RPMs aren't uploaded. The timeout is 55 minutes. ember.spec: 'Release: %{?ember_release}%{!?ember_release:1}%{?dist}'. rpm.sh validates EMBER_RPM_RELEASE. Nothing changed in round 2.
findings.test: packaging.test.ts 'staging in CI': '…upgrades, verifies and removes both RPMs, keeping the admin's policy (review #207)' and 'lets rpm.sh build another release…' failed before and pass now. The job itself runs only in CI (no rpmbuild or dnf here). actionlint passes.

findings.how: Round 1: policy.example.json gained features.wsl and features.ssh (true) and 'commands': {local, wsl, ssh: 'on'}. A new packaging/policy.README is installed beside it by the RPM. It says where the file goes, that a policy without 'commands' turns commands off, that JSON takes no comment key, the lockdown older Embers apply, and one line per key. Round 2, verifier #208: I took the first option. The example's 'ssh' is now {"desktop": true}, with no allowedHosts. main.ts:372 marks SSH as limited whenever allowedHosts is set, even to ["*"], so the copied example would have shown 'only some computers'. policy.README now says the example leaves allowedHosts out so Ember may connect to every computer, and gives the allowedHosts form to copy: "ssh": { "allowedHosts": ["build-*.example.com", "deploy@db-01.example.com:22"], "desktop": true }. I didn't touch main.ts:372 (see notes).
findings.test: packaging.test.ts 'ships an example policy that takes the current keys, so copying it as-is turns nothing off (review #208, #37)' now asserts loaded.policy.ssh equals {desktop: true} with allowedHosts undefined, and that the README shows the allowedHosts form. findings.how: Round 1: LICENCE_TEXTS and suppliedLicence in licences.mjs. Texts are checked in under packaging/licences/: MIT for the GitHub Copilot SDK and runtime packages; Apache-2.0 for sherpa-onnx, plus what its WebAssembly holds, with ONNX Runtime's MIT text; eSpeak NG's GPL-3 COPYING. koffi's platform builds use koffi's LICENSE.txt. Staging stops for any other bundled package without a licence file, and for a sherpa-onnx other than 1.13.8. Round 2, verifier #211: ember.spec's License: tag now includes GPL-3.0-or-later. Its comment says sherpa-onnx's WebAssembly also holds ONNX Runtime and piper-phonemize (MIT), Protocol Buffers and RE2 (BSD-3-Clause), and eSpeak NG (GPL-3.0-or-later), part of a text-to-speech Ember never calls. BUNDLED_LIBRARIES now takes an 'embedded' map: libraries built into a package's binaries that no README table lists. A sherpa-onnx entry lists the 12 libraries the 1.13.8 .wasm holds, with their SPDX ids, and uncoveredLicences checks each against the tag. The d.mts types were updated: libraries and embedded are both optional. A real Linux staging run passes the check. OWNER DECISION NEEDED (legal): Ember redistributes GPL-3.0 object code (eSpeak NG inside sherpa-onnx-wasm-nodejs.wasm). Either meet GPL-3.0 §6, by shipping or offering in writing the corresponding source of the eSpeak NG (and piper-phonemize) that sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 builds in, or ship a sherpa-onnx WebAssembly built without text-to-speech (SHERPA_ONNX_ENABLE_TTS=OFF), which drops eSpeak NG. I have done neither.
findings.test: licences.test.ts 'checks the libraries sherpa-onnx's WebAssembly holds, eSpeak NG's GPL among them (review #211)'. It failed before ([] instead of ["sherpa-onnx's eSpeak NG (GPL-3.0-or-later)"]) and passes now. It also checks that the real spec covers it and that the comment names eSpeak NG with GPL-3.0-or-later. The round 1 licence-text cases still pass.

commits.subject: Keep Ember's windows working when its folder's name has a % in it
Compile the UI Automation bridge by literal path, so brackets in Ember's folder work
Stop the AppImage's doctor failing the sandbox on hosts with user namespaces off
Say Ember needs the desktop session when it is started without a display
Stop staging an Ember whose SSH or command helpers weren't built
Remove the unused second SSH client row, which disagreed with the doctor's
Delete the Node archives of versions Ember no longer pins from the remote runtime cache
Ship an example policy that keeps commands, WSL and SSH on, with notes beside it
Tell whoever upgrades the RPM that a running Ember must be started again
Ship licence texts for the bundled packages that carry none, and stop staging without one
Build the speech models RPM in CI, and upgrade, verify and remove both RPMs there
Run the SSH, WSL and commands suites on pull requests, main and release tags, with RHEL 8's client
Leave allowedHosts out of the example policy, so copying it doesn't say SSH is limited
Name eSpeak NG's GPL-3.0-or-later in the RPM's licence, and check sherpa-onnx's libraries when staging
Load Ember's pages by a URL that writes % as %25, so they load from a folder named like 50%AB
Start the AppImage without Chromium's sandbox where Debian's userns switch is off too
Offer to restart Ember when an update replaced its files while it was running
Say plainly in the policy notes that the example leaves allowedHosts out

docs/DEVELOPING.md §13, replace the sentences from "CI builds both packages on `rockylinux:8`" through "filled the account's artifact storage." with: "CI builds Ember's RPM, the speech models RPM (from the cached, checksum-verified models) and the AppImage on `rockylinux:8`, checks every binary against glibc 2.28, installs the RPM with `dnf`, checks the installed binary's fuses (no debugger, `NODE_OPTIONS` ignored), runs `ember doctor` and starts the installed Ember as a normal user. It then installs the speech models RPM, runs `rpm -V` on both, writes an administrator's `/etc/ember/policy.json`, rebuilds both as Release 2 (`EMBER_RPM_RELEASE=2 scripts/package/rpm.sh`), upgrades to them with `dnf upgrade`, runs `rpm -V` again, checks `chrome-sandbox` is still setuid root and removes both with `rpm -e`. It fails if `/opt/ember`, `/usr/share/ember`, `/usr/bin/ember`, the menu entry or `/usr/share/doc/ember` is left, or if the policy changed or belongs to a package. It uploads Release 1's packages only when asked (§13): **Actions › ci › Run workflow** with **packages** ticked (kept 3 days); at about 450 MB a run with the speech models, uploading them every time filled the account's artifact storage."

For the lead and owner:
(1) #211 needs a legal decision. Ember's packages redistribute GPL-3.0-or-later object code: eSpeak NG inside sherpa-onnx-wasm-nodejs.wasm 1.13.8. The tag, notices and staging check now say so honestly. The owner must either meet GPL-3.0 §6 (ship, or offer in writing, the corresponding source of the eSpeak NG and piper-phonemize that sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 builds in) or switch to a sherpa-onnx WebAssembly built with SHERPA_ONNX_ENABLE_TTS=OFF. Ember uses only keyword spotting, voice activity detection and speech recognition.
(2) #208: a separate small issue remains in main.ts:372 (hot file, not this package's). sshHostsLimited is policy.ssh?.allowedHosts !== undefined, so an administrator who writes allowedHosts: [\"*\"] still sees \"only some computers\". The shipped example no longer triggers it. The one-line fix would be sshHostsLimited: !!list && !list.includes(\"*\"), if the owner of main.ts wants it.
(3) #203: the restart offer comes up as a window is created after an update. That first window may already load the new pages before the user answers. Holding the load back fully would need a gate before every new BrowserWindow, because preloads are read at creation. The question can be asked of the windows created at start too, but only after a change, so it never fires at start-up.
(4) #200 changed every window factory from loadFile to loadURL(pageUrl(...)). Other packages' tests that fake BrowserWindow need loadURL rather than loadFile. I updated the 10 existing fakes. Any new fake another package adds with only loadFile would make that window's load throw in its test.
(5) Scratch evidence is under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/fx-packaging/: pct-probe/, run-pct.sh, pct-before.log, pct-after.log, update-run.sh, upd-first-{keep,replace}.log and the r2-*.log check logs.

verifierProblems.what: The new example policy contains "ssh": {"allowedHosts": ["*"], "desktop": true}. main.ts:372 sets sshHostsLimited whenever policy.ssh?.allowedHosts !== undefined, and computers-copy.ts:141 then shows SSH_LIMITED. So an administrator who copies the example as-is gets "Your organisation lets Ember connect only to some computers." in the Computers tab, even though ["*"] allows every computer. That contradicts policy.README ("[\"*\"] allows every computer") and the fix's own aim that copying the file restricts nothing. Before the change this line never appeared for the example. Same for #37, which shares the file.
verifierProblems.fix: Take allowedHosts out of policy.example.json (keep "ssh": {"desktop": true}) and show the allowedHosts form only in policy.README. Or, if the key must stay, make main.ts:372 treat a list that contains "*" as unlimited (sshHostsLimited: !!list && !list.includes("*")), as a small shared hunk with a unit case. Then add an assertion to the packaging.test.ts example-policy case that the example doesn't mark SSH as limited.

verifierProblems.what: The fix found, and its supplied text says, that sherpa-onnx-wasm-nodejs.wasm 1.13.8 contains eSpeak NG under GPL-3.0-or-later. I confirmed it: strings in the .wasm include 'The specified espeak-ng voice does not exist' and 'use espeak for %s'. It ships the GPL text in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. But packaging/rpm/ember.spec's License: tag (line 26) and its comment still give sherpa-onnx as Apache-2.0 only, and BUNDLED_LIBRARIES has no sherpa-onnx entry, so uncoveredLicences can't flag it. Ember never calls the text-to-speech part, but it still redistributes GPL-3.0 object code, and that brings source-offer obligations nobody has decided on.
verifierProblems.fix: Add GPL-3.0-or-later to the main package's License: tag and to the spec comment. Add a BUNDLED_LIBRARIES entry for sherpa-onnx (eSpeak NG: GPL-3.0-or-later) so staging enforces it. Raise it with the owner in the report: either meet GPL-3.0 §6 (offer the corresponding source for the eSpeak NG in that .wasm) or ship a sherpa-onnx build without text-to-speech.

verifierProblems.what: The reported case is gone: a folder like '100% Free' now works. A real Electron 44.5 window with a sandboxed preload, loaded from 'Tools C# 100% Free (x86) & Zoë's [x]', reports senderFrame.url '...100%%20Free...'. The old check throws URIError on it; the new one returns true. A % followed by two hex digits still breaks Ember another way, though. loadFile from a folder named '50%AB' fails with ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (-6), because Chromium decodes %AB, so Ember's windows stay blank there. The new unit case asserts isTrustedSender('file:///opt/50%AB/...') === true for a URL Ember can never actually load.
verifierProblems.fix: In windows.ts, load the bundled pages with loadURL(pathToFileURL(file).href) (keeping any query or hash) instead of loadFile, so Chromium never decodes a literal %. isTrustedSender's undecoded check still matches '/renderer/' with %25 in the path. Add an Electron or smoke case for a '50%AB' folder. If the hot-file change is out of scope, list '%XX' folder names as a known limitation and drop or relabel the 50%AB unit case.

verifierProblems.what: AppRun (scripts/package/appimage.sh) adds --no-sandbox only when /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces is 0. doctor-probes.ts also sets userNamespaces=false when kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone is 0 (Debian and some hardened Ubuntu). On such a host the AppImage starts without --no-sandbox and Chromium aborts, because the AppImage has no setuid helper. Yet `sudo ./Ember.AppImage doctor` (root adds --no-sandbox) now prints warn 'Ember runs without Chromium's sandbox here…' and 'Ember can work.', which is wrong. The old code reported FAIL in this case.
verifierProblems.fix: Use the same test in AppRun as the probe: also treat `cat /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone` = 0 as user namespaces off before adding --no-sandbox. Alternatively, give the doctor the warn only when max_user_namespaces is 0. Add a launcher test with a stand-in /proc value, or a doctorChecks case.
